question.problem:
Which of the following statements are true?

I. $\text{gcd}(243,167)=3$

II. $\text{gcd}(243,167)=1$

III. $243$ and $167$ are coprime
question.worked_solution:
Recall that two integers are coprime if their greatest common divisor is $1.$ 

With that in mind, let's examine our statements in turn.

- Statement I is false, while statement II is true. Indeed, let's use the Euclidean algorithm, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}243 & = & 167\cdot 1 & + & 76 \\  & ↙ &  & ↙ &  \\ 167 & = & 76\cdot 2 & + & 15 \\  & ↙ &  & ↙ &  \\ 76 & = & 15\cdot 5 & + & 1 \\  & ↙ &  & ↙ &  \\ 15 & = & 15\cdot 1 & + & 0\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

The last positive remainder is $1.$ So, the greatest common divisor of $243$ and $167$ is $1:$

$$
\text{gcd}(243,167)=1.
$$

- Statement III is true. Since $\text{gcd}(243,167)=1,$ the numbers are coprime.

Therefore, the correct answer is "II and III only."

choices.value: None of the statements are true
